transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-04
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood CSM); Alex Chen (NexaHealth Head of ML), Priya Rao (Platform Eng), Diego Martinez (Security)

Summary:
Short sync to review onboarding progress, confirm access for staging environment, review early results from initial embedding/QA runs, and align next steps for benchmarking dedicated capacity. Some discussion on security controls (KMS, SOC2) and latency/cost tradeoffs.

Topics: onboarding status, access setup, perf testing plan, security review items, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we got Alex, Priya, Diego from NexaHealth, and Jordan and I from Redwood, plus Samir. Can you hear me okay?
[00:08] Alex: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks, Maya.
[00:10] Priya: All good here.
[00:12] Diego: Good morning.
[00:15] Maya: Cool. Agenda: onboarding status, access handoff for staging, quick look at the first week of results on embeddings + reranking, and then security items and scheduling a perf run. Anything to add?
[00:25] Alex: That sounds right. We also wanted to flag the timeline — our execs want a go/no-go decision by mid-November, so we need to get bench results in next week.
[00:35] Maya: Understood. Jordan, want to lead the results part?
[00:38] Jordan: Yeah sure. Quick context — we ran the initial embedding batch on the staging snapshots you shared, Priya, and did a small rerank flow for the search quality check. Results are preliminary but suggest the open model variant we shipped does about ~3-5% better NDCG on your sample queries compared to the off-the-shelf baseline you sent. Caveats: sample size small, and there was some tokenization mismatch for a couple documents.
[01:05] Alex: Good, 3-5% is promising. Can you remind us which model variant this was and what infra you used?
[01:12] Jordan: This was redwood-open-1-embedding for embeddings and redwood-opt-7b for rerank, running on our hosted dedicated test pool with 2x A100-equivalents. We used the default quant profile for the reranker to keep costs reasonable.
[01:26] Priya: We noticed higher tail latency on some queries, ~1.2s 95th. Is that from batching or cold KV cache?
[01:34] Jordan: Good question — looks like a combination. In the test run we didn't have prefix caching enabled for the rerank paths and batching was modest, so the tail came from some long-doc attention and a cache miss. For production we recommend enabling KV prefix caching and a small continuous-batch window to smooth the tail. That should bring 95th down closer to 700-800ms in your traffic profile.
[01:55] Diego: On the security front, we need clarity on key management — does Redwood use customer-managed KMS in the Private deployment? We can't have customer data keys stored in Redwood-managed KMS for regulated data.
[02:07] Maya: Yes, for Redwood Private we do support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integration) and the control plane can be configured so key material stays in your account. For the hosted POC we'll use encrypted-at-rest defaults, but we can wire a CMK if you move to a private demo.
[02:22] Diego: Okay that's helpful. For the staging perf run though, we'll still want audit logs and SSO. How are those surfaced?
[02:30] Jordan: We expose audit logs via the console and can stream them to your logging endpoint — S3, Splunk, or a SIEM. SSO is SAML/SCIM for RBAC; we can add the NexaHealth groups you share.
[02:40] Priya: I'll send the group mappings after this call.
[02:43] Alex: About access — Priya was going to set up VPC peering and a service account, is that ready?
[02:50] Priya: Almost. I have the VPC CIDR and a tentative peering config, but I still need the IP ranges for the Redwood staging endpoints and the service account email we should allow. If you share those, I can complete peering tonight.
[03:02] Maya: I'll email the staging endpoint CIDR and the service account address in the next hour. Jordan, do you have the exact IPs?
[03:08] Jordan: I'll pull them from the staging environment, yes. Also I'll include a minimal IAM policy template for the service account so permissions are least-privilege.
[03:17] Alex: Great. Back to perf: we want a controlled run that mimics our peak daytime traffic — about 200 qps for the embedding pipeline and 50 qps for rerank, with 99th latency targets < 1.5s. Can Redwood run that in staging?
[03:31] Jordan: Yes, we can. Two options: run on hosted dedicated test capacity to mirror your expected Dedicated config, or run within your Private staging (if you want keys in your account). For speed of results we typically do a hosted dedicated run first, then repeat in Private if needed.
[03:45] Priya: For the decision next week we just need the hosted dedicated numbers; doing the private run can wait until later.
[03:52] Maya: Ok we will plan hosted dedicated perf test first. Jordan will own bench script and timings.
[03:57] Diego: Couple security asks: 1) provide SOC2 Type II report or portal access, 2) confirm data retention and delete-on-demand, 3) define network egress controls.
[04:08] Maya: We have SOC2 docs — I'll drop the latest report and our security whitepaper. Retention: by default logs are 30 days on hosted, but we can configure retention policies and export/delete workflows for the POC. Egress controls: we can restrict egress to your VPC ranges for Private; for hosted we can provide network allowlists and encrypted transport.
[04:26] Diego: Please include the retention/export steps in that doc.
[04:29] Maya: Will do.
[04:31] Alex: One operational question — what's the suggested quantization profile if we want to reduce cost but keep rerank quality? We tested int8 and saw some small quality drop.
[04:40] Jordan: For rerank we recommend an 8-bit aware quant that keeps important attention kernels in float16; Redwood Optimize suggests a mixed strategy — int8 for MLP weights, fp16 for attention, which tends to preserve quality while reducing GPU memory and cost. We can run a quality regression test as part of the bench to measure NDCG delta before we recommend the final profile.
[05:00] Priya: That regression test would be helpful. Also, any SDK changes we need for the prefix caching or is this handled server-side?
[05:08] Jordan: Mostly server-side, but we'll give you a small SDK flag to opt-into async prefix caching and a sample for keystore rotation.
[05:15] Priya: Perfect.
[05:17] Maya: Quick note on billing for the POC — since you'll run dedicated perf tests, we'll provide a temporary credit for the run and then bill toward committed reserved capacity if you convert. I'll include the pricing slide in the email.
[05:30] Alex: Sounds fair.
[05:33] Jordan: Next, small snag we saw — two documents in your sample had special characters and the tokenizer mapped them oddly, producing joined tokens that affected rerank. Suggest normalization pre-ingest, we can share a small script.
[05:46] Priya: We can patch the ETL quickly. Please send the normalization script.
[05:50] Jordan: Will do, sharing via the shared drive link.
[05:53] Maya: I'll recap next steps in the notes and assign owners. Anything else from Nexa?
[05:58] Alex: No, that's it. Appreciate the fast turnaround.
[06:01] Diego: One more ask — can you include a sample SOC2 security contact and a primary support path for escalations?
[06:08] Samir: Yes, Diego, I'll include our security contact and the premium support escalation path in the email.
[06:14] Priya: Great.
[06:16] Maya: Ok, we'll run with the plan: Jordan produces scripts and perf runbook, Maya sends pricing + SOC2 + SOW, Priya provides peering and service account, Diego confirms KMS/retention constraints. We'll target the perf run on 2026-11-10.
[06:33] Alex: Thank you everyone.
[06:35] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email.
[06:38] (call ends)

References and shared artifacts:
- Staging endpoints & CIDR (to be emailed)
- Perf benchmark script (Jordan to share): https://redwood.example.com/shared/nexa/perf-script
